UPSTREAM: mb/google/hatch: Bump up the BIOS region to 28MiB This change bumps up the BIOS region to 28MiB to use the hole between SI_ALL and SI_BIOS. Since this SPI flash part is 32MiB, only the top 16MiB actually gets memory mapped. Thus, the change ensures that only RW_LEGACY lies in the 12MiB that is not memory mapped. BUG=b:123443737 TEST=Verified that hatch still boots up. Ensured that fmap dump looks correct. chromeos-base: Address system_api race and missing slot operators. There is a race in incremental-paladin between system_api being recompiled with the new protoc and its dependencies being rebuilt with the new protobuf library. This addresses the problem by incrementing the slot of system_api and making sure the := slot operator is used where appropriate. BUG=chromium:931746 TEST=the protobuf uprev makes it through the CQ. Reland "libbrillo: add DevmapperTable and DeviceMapper" This is a reland of c1675c3e2e91f65ce557d5763d52e49ab7021178 The original patch used SecureBlob contents unsafely (out-of-bounds access). Instead of using C-string, use a StringTokenizer to parse the contents of the string data in SecureBlob. The string tokenizer only uses pointers to find tokens and hence doesn't leak memory. Reason for revert: chromium:887667 Original change's description: > libbrillo: add DevmapperTable and DeviceMapper > > blkdev_utils implements utilities to setup block devices. > This patch adds a libdevmapper-based DeviceMapper implementation > to blkdev_utils. DeviceMapper supports the minimal operations > required to manage dm-verity or dm-crypt devices. > > * The bulk of the operations are implemented using DevmapperTasks, > which are analogous to libdevmapper dm_task structs. > > * DevmapperTable allows easier handling of I/O to the libdevmapper > interface. > > * DeviceMapper uses a DevmapperTaskFactory to create tasks, which > can be overriden with a different implementation (eg. based on > ProcessImpl) or a fake implementation (eg. FakeDevmapperTask). > > * Add Blob <--> SecureHex conversions for the secure conversions. > > (Additional review context: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/983059) > > BUG=chromium:808303 > CQ-DEPEND=CL:1222791 > TEST=FEATURES=TEST emerge libbrillo > > Change-Id: Ib93d0ed7056a0cb49d2a8895f34adca9862698ed > Signed-off-by: Sarthak Kukreti <sarthakkukreti@chromium.org> > Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1187155 > Commit-Ready: Gwendal Grignou <gwendal@chromium.org> > Tested-by: Gwendal Grignou <gwendal@chromium.org> > Reviewed-by: Gwendal Grignou <gwendal@chromium.org> BUG=chromium:808303,chromium:887667 CQ-DEPEND=CL:1459497,CL:1459498 TEST=unit tests. FROMGIT: drm/i915: rename CNP_RAWCLK_FRAC to CNP_RAWCLK_DEN Although CNP names this field "Counter Fraction", what we write to the register is really the denominator for the fractional part of the divider, not the fractional part (and the field description even says that). The ICP spec renamed the field to "Counter Fraction Denominator", which makes a lot more sense. Use the more complete ICL naming because we will merge the CNP and ICP functions into a single one, which will introduce the concept of the numerator. That will make a lot more sense when you read the "num/frac = den" calculation. Reviewed-by: Ville Syrjl <ville.syrjala@linux.intel.com> Signed-off-by: Paulo Zanoni <paulo.r.zanoni@intel.com> Link: https://patchwork.freedesktop.org/patch/msgid/20181112232313.26373-2-paulo.r.zanoni@intel.com (cherry-picked from commit 228a5cf381f761ca16ef6b31b24c4533594468bd git://anongit.freedesktop.org/drm-intel drm-intel-next-queued) BUG=b:123552464 TEST=HDMI EDID clock should be less than 100KHz Change-Id: Ide1c26ee98dc8f77f80d2f086cc32bf79427ed0a Signed-off-by: Khaled Almahallawy <khaled.almahallawy@intel.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1455361 Commit-Ready: Abhay Kumar <abhay.kumar@intel.com> Tested-by: Abhay Kumar <abhay.kumar@intel.com> Reviewed-by: Sean Paul <seanpaul@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Stéphane Marchesin <marcheu@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Abhay Kumar <abhay.kumar@intel.com>

cros-rust: Clean up env var handling Clean up environment variable handling so that they are all exported in the src_configure function rather than being exported in an ad hoc way all over the eclass. Packages that use this eclass are now always built with debuginfo=2, optlevel=3, and link-time optimization. Integer overflow checks are also enabled by default as they should have a trivial performance impact on most binaries. Packages that are drastically affected by the overflow checks can set CROS_RUST_OVERFLOW_CHECKS=0 to disable this option. Overflow checks and debug assertions are still always enabled when the cros-debug USE flag is set. Also clean up the rustflag handling and export rustflags in src_configure. This should make it possible to build binaries and run tests with sanitizers enabled without restricting them to fuzzers. pd: Don't Try.Src if battery is disconnected. If a battery is disconnected (the discharge FET is disabled) we should not attempt Try.Src even though the battery state of charge may be above CONFIG_USB_PD_TRY_SRC_MIN_BATT_SOC. The reason is that in this case, the battery is not providing charge to the system, so attempting Try.Src will temporarily cut VBUS which may be the only power source in the system at this time. This commit simply checks the battery disconnect state when deciding to attempt Try.Src. gcc: allow us to force -Wno-error in builds For testing LLVM/clang nearer to ToT, it's useful if new warnings aren't fatal. This allows us to set a special environment variable to get a final say in the fatalness of warnings. Tweaking CFLAGS/CXXFLAGS isn't sufficient because we want warnings to never be fatal for these builds, and it's trivial for a single ebuild to place its own -Werror (or similar) after the user-provided CFLAGS/CXXFLAGS. This behavior is desirable for things that rely on -Werror like autotools, but not great in the case of projects like Chrome or things in platform2. More importantly, we have plans for building extra tooling on top of this support. Please see bug 914081 for more about that. BUG=chromium:903652, chromium:914081 TEST=emerged cross-gcc and built packages that should've otherwise had fatal warnings. Needed a separate hook to actually `export` the variable, naturally. login: Unthrottle cpu quota for ARC on system login This change resets the cpu quota for ARC i.e. gives it the maximum CPU quota whenever a login happens. Previously, a login and logout would just use the last CPU quota value set by Chrome for ARC. This would cause ARC boot with CL:1324972 to be extremely slow on the next login in case it was throttled right before the last logout. BUG=b:118696077 TEST=Manual testing and cheets_AuthPerf autotest. cryptohome: Support either-of-PCRs for TPM2 signature sealing Update the TPM2 signature sealing backend to support restrictions "the PCRs should be in either of the specified states", e.g. "(PCRx==foo && PCRy==bar) OR (PCRx==bar && PCRz==baz)". This paves the way for supporting the feature "allow login only when specified PCRs are either in the default or in the user-specific states" for challenge-response protected cryptohomes (a.k.a. smart card login).
